stories.headline: 13 arrested in multi-agency child sex trafficking sting across Denver metro
stories.summary:
More than a dozen men from across the Denver metro area were arrested following a monthslong undercover investigation targeting child sex offenders, Aurora police announced. The operation, dubbed SAFE Kids, was partly spurred by the passage of Colorado Senate Bill 26-15, which elevated internet luring of a child for commercial sexual activity to a Class 3 felony and established mandatory minimum prison sentences of 4 to 12 years.

Detectives began planning the operation in May, identifying websites where child internet luring and human trafficking activity takes place. Starting in mid-August, undercover officers posed as minors online and arranged encounters with suspects, several of whom arrived with sexual devices, drugs, alcohol, or a firearm. Among the 13 suspects — ranging in age from 21 to 65 — two were already registered sex offenders.

Charges against the suspects include patronizing a prostituted child, solicitation, internet luring of a child, and attempted sexual assault of a child. Aurora Police Lt. Seth Robertson said the operation underscores the importance of proactive police work in exposing crimes that occur behind closed doors and out of public view.

stories.headline: Denver police discover suspected drug lab during death investigation in Baker neighborhood
stories.summary:
Denver Police officers uncovered a suspected homemade drug lab while responding to a death investigation early Tuesday morning on the edge of the Baker and Lincoln Park neighborhoods, the department said. Few details about the death or the nature of the suspected lab were immediately released.

The discovery raises concerns about the intersection of illegal drug manufacturing and fatal incidents in central Denver neighborhoods. Police have not announced any arrests in connection with the lab or the death as of Tuesday.

stories.headline: 8-year-old boy found safe in Sheridan after Amber Alert issued for Arvada abduction
stories.summary:
An 8-year-old boy was found safe Tuesday morning shortly after law enforcement issued an Amber Alert reporting him missing from Arvada. The boy's grandfather had taken him from an apartment in the 9000 block of Oberon Road at about 9:30 a.m., with authorities believing the two were headed toward Grand Junction in a truck.

Sheridan and Englewood police located the boy with his grandfather in Sheridan approximately 10 minutes after the alert was issued. The grandfather was arrested and is facing multiple charges, according to Arvada police spokesman David Snelling.

stories.headline: E-bike rider dies after collision with vehicle in Centennial
stories.summary:
An e-bike rider died Monday from injuries sustained in a Sunday crash with a vehicle near East Orchard Road and South Telluride Street in Centennial, the Arapahoe County Sheriff's Office announced Tuesday. The woman, whose name and age had not been released pending autopsy and family notification, was taken to a hospital in critical condition following the crash and did not survive.

The driver of the vehicle remained at the scene and is cooperating with investigators. The Sheriff's Office Traffic Safety Unit is continuing its investigation, and no decision on potential criminal charges had been made as of Tuesday. The crash briefly closed westbound Orchard Road between Tower Road and Buckley Road.

stories.headline: Foreign hackers breached two small Colorado water utilities in August, altered pump settings and disabled alarms
stories.summary:
Foreign hackers breached two small Colorado water utilities last month, changing equipment settings, disabling remote access and alarms, and altering pumping cycles, Gov. Jared Polis' office confirmed Tuesday. The two affected providers are small, private utilities each serving fewer than 200 people, and officials said treatment processes and water quality were not impacted.

The governor's spokeswoman Ally Sullivan said Colorado cannot confirm which foreign actors were involved but cited ongoing national efforts by an Iranian-backed group to access drinking water and wastewater systems, as documented by the federal Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. The revelation came one day after UCHealth officials disclosed that someone had intentionally disrupted the oxygen supply at Colorado's largest hospital earlier this month.

The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment followed up with each provider and reached out to other utilities statewide to prevent similar incidents. MSU Denver cybersecurity professor Steve Beaty warned that smaller utilities are particularly vulnerable due to limited staffing and resources, and that attacks on smaller targets can be a precursor to strikes on larger infrastructure.

stories.headline: Aspen-Pitkin County Airport evacuated, briefly closed after email threat; reopens within hours
stories.summary:
The Aspen-Pitkin County Airport was evacuated and closed for more than an hour Tuesday afternoon after staff received an email threat regarding airport property, airport spokesperson Kelsey Petersen said. About 55 passengers, 40 airline employees, and additional TSA and rental car personnel were evacuated at approximately 2:30 p.m. Law enforcement inspected the facility before clearing it, and the terminal reopened at about 4 p.m.

A SkyWest Airlines flight scheduled to land in Aspen at around 3 p.m. was rerouted back to Denver before eventually heading back to Aspen. Petersen declined to provide further details about the nature of the threat, citing an ongoing investigation. Colorado 82 remained open in both directions throughout the closure.

stories.headline: Waymo's arrival in Denver raises questions about competition with financially struggling RTD
stories.summary:
The Regional Transportation District is facing a new competitor as Waymo's autonomous robotaxis begin operating across a 60-square-mile service area in Denver this month. RTD already faces a $215 million structural deficit projected to hit in 2027, and board directors recently passed a directive to explore $20 million in bus service cuts — a move that drew criticism given the agency's simultaneous commitment of more than $200 million toward the Front Range Passenger Rail project.

Research from Waymo's other markets shows that its pricing has narrowed significantly toward other ride-hailing services over just a few years, potentially placing it in more direct competition with transit over time. RTD ridership data shows that its remaining riders are increasingly transit-dependent, with a growing share of low-income households owning fewer cars compared to a decade ago.

District Director Chris Nicholson said he views autonomous vehicles like Waymo as an additional leg in a broader transportation network rather than a direct threat. However, critics and transit advocates warn that if Waymo draws away riders who have other options, it could deepen RTD's financial spiral ahead of a potential public tax revenue request in 2028.

stories.headline: Outside groups pour $3 million into Colorado ballot measure campaigns in two-week period
stories.summary:
Issue committees supporting and opposing several Colorado ballot measures reported spending more than $3 million combined between Sept. 3 and Sept. 16, according to campaign finance reports filed Monday. The largest spender was the Colorado Voter Trust Initiative, which backed Amendment 84 — a proposed constitutional amendment that would require voters to include their Social Security number or driver's license number on mail ballot return envelopes — reporting $2 million in spending during the period and more than $3.3 million for the full cycle.

Yes for Colorado Kids, which supports Proposition NN — a measure that would allow the state to keep tax revenue above TABOR limits for education — spent $715,000, bringing its total to more than $1.2 million. Coloradans for Real Safety Solutions, opposing an Advance Colorado proposal to increase criminal penalties for fentanyl possession, spent $426,000 during the period and nearly $700,000 overall.

On the legislative candidate side, the Republican Senate Majority Fund reported spending nearly $1 million to defend a GOP-held Senate seat and target two Democratic-held seats in Pueblo and Loveland. Democrats currently hold near-supermajority margins in both chambers, and control of several swing districts could determine whether Republicans avoid superminority status after November.

stories.headline: Gov. Polis mourns death of 'first dog' Gia, a fixture of his eight-year tenure
stories.summary:
Gia, the dog who was a near-constant companion to Gov. Jared Polis throughout his eight years leading Colorado, died Monday at age 17. Polis announced her passing on Facebook, writing: "She was our everything — an amazing dog who loved us unconditionally."

Polis and his husband Marlon Reis adopted Gia in August 2009 from an Englewood shelter during Polis' first year as a U.S. representative. She accompanied Polis to bill signings, news conferences, cabinet meetings, and events across the state, and was featured in a 2025 Rocky Mountain PBS documentary about dogs at the Colorado Capitol.

Gia even appeared at Polis and Reis' 2021 wedding, leaving her paw prints on the marriage certificate. With Polis set to leave office in January, Gia was by his side for nearly his entire public career.

stories.headline: First day of fall brings sun to Denver, with heavy rain and storms possible Wednesday through Thursday
stories.summary:
The autumnal equinox arrived just after 6 p.m. Mountain Time Tuesday, officially closing out summer for the Denver metro. Scattered showers and thunderstorms were moving through parts of the region Tuesday night, with mostly cloudy skies expected after midnight.

A more active weather pattern is set to arrive Wednesday, with surging moisture and a disturbance expected to trigger a higher chance for showers and thunderstorms Wednesday evening and overnight. Heavy rain is the primary concern, particularly across the eastern plains, with Denver also in line for potentially soaking rainfall.

Thursday morning is expected to be the wettest stretch of the week, with highs dropping to the upper 60s to low 70s. Conditions are forecast to improve Friday and through the weekend, with highs rebounding to the low-to-mid 80s before another potential storm system arrives by the following Tuesday.

stories.headline: Western Slope gas prices among Colorado's highest; Denver ozone season one of worst in 30 years
stories.summary:
Coloradans are paying widely varying prices at the pump depending on where they live, with the Western Slope recording some of the highest gas prices in the state, according to CPR News. More than 80 percent of all fuel consumed in Colorado passes through the Denver Metro Northern Front Range terminal, giving the metro area structural pricing advantages over more remote regions.

The report also noted that metro Denver and the northern Front Range experienced one of the worst ozone pollution seasons in the past 30 years this summer, jeopardizing the region's standing under federal air quality standards. That could place additional financial burdens on area businesses subject to emissions regulations.

stories.headline: National analysts move Broncos up in power rankings after Week 2 comeback win over Jaguars
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos improved their national standing in NFL power rankings following their 20-13 home-opener comeback victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars, with multiple analysts highlighting the team's defensive resilience and the emergence of wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and rookie running back Jonah Coleman. Coleman led the Broncos with 39 rushing yards on 10 carries, scored his first NFL touchdown, and celebrated with the Mile High Salute made famous by Terrell Davis.

Analysts noted ongoing concerns, however, including Bo Nix's slow starts — he has thrown eight of his 23 career interceptions in September — and Denver being flagged for 17 penalties across the first two games of the season. The Broncos rallied from 10 points down in the fourth quarter to secure the win.

Denver next hosts the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football at 6:20 p.m. The game will be the team's second consecutive home game and the first prime-time appearance of the 2026 season.

topStory.headline: Trump Addresses UN General Assembly, Urges Putin to End Ukraine War as Iran Tensions Persist
topStory.summary:
President Donald Trump arrived in New York for the United Nations General Assembly session, where he briefly addressed reporters and delivered a pointed message regarding the ongoing war in Ukraine. When asked what he would say to Russian President Vladimir Putin, Trump responded with two words: 'Settle the war.' Trump and First Lady Melania Trump then proceeded into the General Assembly session.

The appearance came amid a broader set of controversies surrounding the Trump administration's foreign policy posture. Trump has claimed credit for resolving multiple international conflicts, including wars involving Israel, Hamas, Iran, and several African nations, though the accuracy of those claims has been disputed. His administration brokered a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, as well as an agreement involving Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo, though fighting in those regions has continued in varying degrees.

Trump has also faced scrutiny over his statements at a separate press conference in New York City, held alongside Mayor Zohran Mamdani, in which he defended the White House's decision to ban CNN, Politico, and MS NOW from press access. During that briefing, Trump cited what he described as major accomplishments the press was failing to cover, including claims that he had 'settled eight wars' and that '$21 trillion' was 'pouring in' to the United States. Neither figure has been substantiated, and news organizations including CNN have repeatedly challenged both claims.

The Russia-Ukraine war, now in its fourth year following Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, remains one of the most significant ongoing conflicts in the world. Trump has previously expressed a desire to negotiate a settlement between Moscow and Kyiv, though no formal peace talks have taken place under his administration. His call on Putin to 'settle the war' at the UN marks one of his most direct public statements on the matter in recent weeks, though no policy details or diplomatic steps were announced alongside the remark.
